# @vllnt/convex-quota

> Experimental scheduled-reset per-subject allowances; not yet released.

Targets Node >=22.12.0 and convex@^1.45.0. One sandboxed allowance row per
(scope, subjectRef, key) stores used, limit, periodKey, policyKey and window times.
Calendar windows support IANA timezones and day/week/month resets; rolling windows
start on first allowed consume; epoch windows align to Unix epoch. A key's window
policy cannot change (POLICY_MISMATCH); limits may change without resetting usage.
Refs/scopes are 1..256 UTF-16 code units. Amounts/limits are positive safe integers.
Durations are positive safe integer milliseconds with safe end timestamps.

consume(ctx, subjectRef, key, limit, window, opts?) returns allowed, used,
remaining, limit, periodKey, resetsAt; opts is {amount?, scope?}.
remaining(ctx, subjectRef, key, limit, window, scope?) returns the same without
allowed. It is a query-execution snapshot: subscriptions do not refresh just
because time passes. consume always rechecks server time.
refund(ctx, subjectRef, key, amount, periodKey, scope?) returns refunded, used,
remaining. Requires matching unexpired stored period; clamps usage at zero.
Consume and refund are NOT idempotent; hosts must deduplicate events. A period
label is not a receipt and can be reused after erasure.
eraseSubject(ctx, subjectRef, scope?, batch?) returns this pass's deletion count;
batches default to 200 and cap at 500, scheduling continuation when full. Hosts
must stop concurrent writes while cleanup drains. No tombstones or audit history.

Host owns auth, authorization and all policy. Multiple named mounts isolate data;
runtime scopes isolate indexed reads/erasure within a mount. Official
@convex-dev/rate-limiter already has fixed windows, token buckets, readable checks
and React hooks; prefer it for general throttling. This experiment's narrower
calendar/timezone/refund boundary still needs independent consumer justification.
Publication is blocked; passing tests alone does not establish adoption or readiness.
